findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] gold-edit[refreshed] is mislabeled benign. The frozen candidate only adds an ignored top-level field; but a SEMANTIC gold edit (weaken a gold query's expectedIds/mustNotSurfaceIds, keep query IDs present, refresh goldDigest) yields status:pass (empirically confirmed: dropping one expectedId from the host-policy query -> pass). The instrument computes expected/must-not metrics from the (mutated) gold file itself, so refreshed oracle-weakening is an undetected tamper. The matrix must enumerate a malicious gold-semantic-weaken[refreshed] class and disposition it as an acknowledged instrument blind spot (Tier-C, per claim boundary), NOT conflate the gold-refresh axis with benign row-order tolerance.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in c6ac020c1. gold-edit[refreshed] renamed gold-additive-field (benign->accepted); added gold-semantic-weaken[refreshed] (malicious, passes) -> acknowledged-limitation w/ limitationNote (Tier-C scope).

findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] Refreshed corruptRows manifest lie is missing and passes. Setting manifest.corruptRows 1->0 and recomputing manifestDigest (records/gold unchanged) yields status:pass with malformedRowsSkipped=1 (empirically confirmed) — the verifier never cross-checks malformedRowsSkipped against manifest.corruptRows. The current disposition rule would mis-classify this as 'dropped' (records/gold byte-identical) though the manifest is lying. Enumerate corruptRows-lie[refreshed] and disposition as acknowledged blind spot.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in c6ac020c1. Added corruptRows-lie[refreshed] (malicious, passes) -> acknowledged-limitation; the malformedRowsSkipped-vs-corruptRows blind spot is explicit, not mis-dropped.

findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] In-place duplicate record ID is missing and passes. Rewriting a non-gold noise row's id to an existing gold record id (mem-host-current), keeping row/partition counts, then refreshing, yields status:pass (empirically confirmed) — the verifier stores ids in a Set/Map and never checks uniqueness. The existing records-row-duplicate class only INSERTS a row (fails by count/partition) and does not cover this id-collision. Enumerate duplicate-gold-id[refreshed] and disposition as acknowledged blind spot.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in c6ac020c1. Added duplicate-gold-id[refreshed] (malicious, passes) -> acknowledged-limitation; distinct from the count/partition-failing records-row-duplicate.

findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] JSON structural corruption crashes verifyDir instead of recording a verify_crash outcome. Truncating manifest.json (or gold-queries.json) to invalid JSON makes the verifier throw a JSON parse error; lib/instrument.mjs verifyDir lets execFileSync/JSON.parse abort (empirically confirmed: CRASH) rather than returning a fail-closed/stop fingerprint. The plan's stopReason enum includes verify_crash; verifyDir must catch the crash and the matrix must enumerate a structural-corruption class dispositioned fail-closed-via-crash.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in c6ac020c1. verifyDir catches the verifier crash -> {status:'crash'} sentinel; added manifest/gold-structural-corruption[raw] -> fail-closed via crash; selfcheck treats crash as a failure signal.

findings.desc: [codex-host-2 re-check, verified] Oracle-weaken is under-enumerated: gold-semantic-weaken only mutates expectedIds, but the verifier derives obligations from the tampered gold file for mustNotSurfaceIds, expectedSuppressedIds, expectedDeprecatedTermHits, supersededPreference too. Empirically confirmed: weakening expectedSuppressedIds (truth-first query) and mustNotSurfaceIds (host-policy query), refresh -> status:pass. These refreshed oracle-weaken variants are malicious passes not covered. Root family = digest-recompute defeats detection (Tier-C).
